title: Build Array from Permutation
description:
# Build Array from Permutation

Given a **zero-based permutation** `nums`, build and return an array `ans` of the same length where `ans[i] = nums[nums[i]]` for every valid index `i`.

A zero-based permutation of length `n` contains every integer from `0` to `n - 1` exactly once. That means every value in `nums` is also a valid index into `nums`, so the nested lookup `nums[nums[i]]` is always defined.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [0,2,1,5,3,4]
**Output:** [0,1,2,4,5,3]
**Explanation:** The answer reads the original array at indices [0,1,2,5,3,4], because those are the values selected by `nums[i]`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [5,0,1,2,3,4]
**Output:** [4,5,0,1,2,3]
**Explanation:** For index 0, the answer is `nums[nums[0]] = nums[5] = 4`; the same rule is applied to every index.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= nums.length <= 1000`
* `0 <= nums[i] < nums.length`
* The elements in `nums` are distinct.

**Follow-up:** Can you solve it without using an extra array other than the returned array, using only `O(1)` extra working memory?

solutions.name: Direct Output Array
solutions.description:
## Approach

Allocate a separate answer array and fill each position directly from the definition `ans[i] = nums[nums[i]]`.

## Key Insight

Because `nums` is a permutation, `nums[i]` is always a valid index. Keeping the output separate is the clearest baseline because no write can corrupt a value that a later position still needs to read.

## Complexity Analysis

The loop visits every index once, so the time complexity is O(n). The returned answer array stores n values, so the space complexity is O(n).

solutions.name: In-Place Modular Encoding
solutions.description:
## Approach

Encode the original value and the new answer value in the same array cell. Since all values are smaller than `n`, store `old + n * new`, then divide by `n` in a second pass to extract the answer.

## Key Insight

When reading `nums[nums[i]]`, the target cell may already be encoded. Taking `% n` recovers its original value, so earlier writes cannot disturb later reads.

## Complexity Analysis

There are two linear passes over the array, so the time complexity is O(n). Apart from the input array itself, only a few integer variables are used, giving O(1) extra working space.

solutions.name: Snapshot Then Rewrite Input
solutions.description:
## Approach

Clone the original permutation first, then rewrite `nums[i]` using only values from that snapshot. The input array becomes the returned answer after the rewrite pass.

## Key Insight

This route teaches the mutation hazard directly: if we overwrite `nums` while still reading from it, later nested lookups can read changed values. A snapshot separates the read source from the write target.

## Complexity Analysis

Cloning and rewriting are both linear operations, so the time complexity is O(n). The snapshot stores n integers, giving O(n) extra space.

solutions.name: Index Stream Mapping
solutions.description:
## Approach

Generate the index range `0..n-1` and map each index to `nums[nums[i]]`, letting the stream collect the mapped values into the returned array.

## Key Insight

The problem is a pure index transformation when the input is not mutated. A stream makes that transformation explicit: each output position depends only on the original permutation and its own index.

## Complexity Analysis

The stream evaluates one mapping per index, so the time complexity is O(n). The produced array contains n values, so the space complexity is O(n).
